Round-robin , paired comparison , or tournament voting methods , are a set of ranked voting systems that choose winners by comparing every pair of candidates one-on-one, similar to a round-robin tournament . [ 1 ] In each paired matchup, the total number of voters who prefer each candidate is recorded in a beats matrix . Then, a majority-preferred (Condorcet) candidate is elected, if one exists. Otherwise, if there is a cyclic tie , the candidate "closest" to being a Condorcet winner is elected, based on the recorded beats matrix. How "closest" is defined varies by method.
